newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Kim hopes for Korean reconciliation.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Kim hopes for Korean reconciliation.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam said he hoped 1997 would see a turning point towards reconciliation between the two Koreas and improved relations between the Seoul government and labour unions.
Kim made the comment in a New Year message days after Pyongyang apologised for a submarine incursion in September that South Korea condemned as a deliberate military provocation.
"It is my earnest hope that this year will bring a turning point toward reconciliation and cooperation in relations with North Korea," Kim said.
"We are all called upon to exert our best to attain peaceful unification of the homeland and enhance national prosperity."
Kim had halted all economic aid to the North pending an apology over the incident.
The North's apology on Sunday -- an unprecedented statement of contrition expressing "deep regret" for the incident -- was followed the next day by vitriolic attacks on South Korea.
It lashed out at "butchers" in Seoul as the ashes of 24 North Koreans shot after landing in the South from the submarine were handed back across the border.
The two Koreas remain technically at war since their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce and not a peace treaty.
Kim said he hoped to see a spirit of reconcilation prevail in the nation's politics and labour relations.
"A selfish preoccupation with narrow personal gains should be dropped in the interest of national development and the happiness of all the people," Kim said.
"The wisdom of reconcilation and compromise between one region and another, between one political party and another and between labour and management needs to be brought into play."

Last week, militant trade union members went on strike across the country after the ruling New Korea Party rammed a new labour law through parliament that gives employers the right to lay off workers, hire temporary workers and replace strikers.
Unionists called off strikes for New Year holidays, but threatened to start up again soon after.
